summary: Trims a section from first-input channels and inserts second-input channels, with stretch/trim/interpolate options and name or index matching.
key_concepts: Splice CHOP inserts channels from the second input into channels from the first input.
Start and Trim Length define where samples are removed from the first input before insertion.
Output Trimmed Section reverses the result and outputs the removed portion instead of the spliced result.
Inserted second-input data can be kept at natural length, stretched to the trim region, trimmed/cycled to insert length, or stretched to insert length.
Channels can be matched by number or name; unmatched channels can fill gaps with none, linear, or cubic interpolation.
The official docs call out edit-and-replace workflows where one Splice extracts a section and another inserts the modified section back at the original index.

common_gotchas: First input supplies the original channels; second input supplies inserted data.
Output Trimmed Section flips the output to the removed region, useful for edit/replace workflows.
Match by name when inserting a modified subset back into a multi-channel CHOP.
Unmatched second-input channels can leave gaps unless interpolation is set deliberately.
Stretching inserted material can smooth or distort timing depending on interpolation mode.
For simple remove-only operations, Delete CHOP or Trim CHOP may be clearer.
For smoothing a region, the docs recommend using an unmatched second input and setting Insert Method plus Insert Interpolate deliberately.
